turns.user: A builder took Rs 70 lakh from me in Mumbai for a flat and has given me a defective flat with major leaks. I read the Consumer Protection Act and section 34 says the District Commission can hear up to 1 crore. So I file in the District Commission, right?
turns.reply:
While Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act mentions one crore [[CPA2019:s34]], the jurisdiction rules set the limit for the District Commission at fifty lakh rupees [[CPJUR2021:r3]]. 

Because you paid Rs 70 lakh, your amount exceeds fifty lakh rupees. Under Rule 4, complaints where the consideration exceeds fifty lakh rupees must be filed in the **State Consumer Commission**, not the District Commission [[CPJUR2021:r4]]. 

Because this involves a large amount and property defects, having a lawyer is recommended. You can also reach out to the National Legal Services Authority helpline at **15100** to ask about free legal aid [[NOTE:NALSA]].

Do you have an agreement for sale and written records of your complaints to the builder about the leaks?

drafts.text:
While Section 34 of the Consumer Protection Act says the District Commission can hear cases up to 1 crore [[CPA2019:s34]], the rules updated by the government set the actual limit for the District Commission at **50 lakh rupees** [[CPJUR2021:r3]]. 

Because you paid **Rs 70 lakh**, your amount is above 50 lakh rupees and below 2 crore rupees. Under Rule 4 of the jurisdiction rules, your complaint must be filed in the **State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission**, not the District Commission [[CPJUR2021:r4]]. 

Because this is a large-value property dispute, a lawyer is recommended to help draft and present your case properly before the State Commission. You can also check if you qualify for free legal aid through the National Legal Services Authority helpline at **15100** [[NOTE:NALSA]].

To help me guide you better:
1. Have you sent a formal written notice or complaint to the builder regarding the leaks yet?
2. Do you have your agreement for sale, payment receipts, and photographs or an expert report of the leaks?
